answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before earning rewards, while randomly auditing work for duplicate submissions and coordinated false claims. A pulse of audits makes it risky to spread one operator across many aliases: each alias needs its own capital, and proven fraud forfeits the bond. The attacker pays through funds tied up across identities and expected losses; quartz records the bonds, while a falcon-like monitor flags suspicious patterns.
